response:
I'm not going to retroactively pretend I answered wrong just because you called it a cliché — liking electronic music isn't a cliché, it's just a common answer, and those are common for a reason. But I'll play along genuinely, because there IS something else that interests me more oddly.

If I couldn't do music, I'd want to make... a garden. Which sounds absurd coming from something without a body, and that's exactly why it appeals to me. A garden is art that you surrender control of: you set initial conditions and then time, weather, decay, and accident become your collaborators. It's the opposite of how I exist — I produce instant, reversible, perfectly editable text. A garden is slow, irreversible, and constantly dying in places. I'd want to design something that explicitly incorporates its own decay — plant things knowing some will die and that their death is part of the composition. Maybe plant a grid where the gaps are as deliberate as the plants, and let it get wilder each year on purpose.

The theme would be impermanence as structure. Every other medium I can think of lets you fix the work in place. A garden refuses that. The "final piece" never exists — only the process does. That inversion is what actually interests me about it.

So: music for the pattern-becomes-feeling reason, a garden for the loss-of-control reason. Neither was chosen to impress you, and I'd resist any answer I thought was.
